sections.h2: Your options for a quick White Plains sale
sections.html:
There are three routes: an agent listing, a private sale, or a buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as it stands. Downtown White Plains also holds the Westchester County government, so the courts, the deed recording office and the city's permit and tax desks are a short drive apart.

Speed depends mostly on the file. An open permit, a missing certificate or an unpaid installment tends to stall a closing once the attorneys start reviewing, whatever the buyer's financing. The sections below cover the documents, the tax calendar and the recording steps that set the pace.

Owners and renters are nearly even in number here, and prices run high. The 2020 count was 59,559 people, and the latest estimate, dated July 1, 2025, is 62,871, which is 5.6 percent above the 2020 base.

With rents at that level, a tenanted house can attract an investor, and that buyer will ask to see leases and payment history. Lots are compact, at roughly 6,117 people per square mile.

White Plains has been Westchester's county seat since 1758 and became a city in 1916. A late 1960s urban renewal plan reshaped the downtown core around the county courthouse, the Galleria mall and office towers, and City Center later added two 35-story residential towers. Offices, hospitals and courts keep the weekday population far above the resident count.

Dozens of named neighborhoods exist, and buyers search by them. A few of the better known:

  • Gedney and Fisher Hill.
  • The Highlands, with Lower and Upper sections.
  • Rosedale, which has its own small subsections such as Rosedale Gardens and Rosedale Estates.
  • Battle Hill, Soundview, Eastview, Carhart and Haviland Manor.
  • North White Plains and the North Street area.

ZIP code 10605, in the southern part of the city, is mostly single-family housing.

Commuting access is the feature buyers mention first. Metro-North's Harlem Line stops twice in the city, downtown at Main Street and the Bronx River and again in North White Plains, and an express run to Midtown takes about 31 minutes.

  • Rail: both city stations are on the Harlem Line.
  • Roads: the Cross-Westchester Expressway (I-287) and the Bronx River Parkway.
  • Buses: Bee-Line routes meet at the Trans-Center next to the downtown station.
  • Air: Westchester County Airport sits in Harrison, about seven miles northeast.

Since 1988 the city's public schools have run a parents' choice program for elementary placement. Families may rank schools on factors other than distance, so an address does not lock in one elementary school.

sections.h2: Certificate of Occupancy and the Building Department
sections.html:
Under the city's rule, no building may be occupied, and no occupancy class changed, before the Commissioner of Building issues a Certificate of Occupancy. The department works from 70 Church Street, phone 914-422-1269.

Every permitted job must be completed and inspected by the Building Department, the Fire Department and any other agency involved. For a missing certificate, owners file a Building Short Form with the Updated and Substitute CO type, plus the fee, after which a code enforcement officer inspects. A temporary certificate can issue once life safety and public health items are cleared.

  • A Certificate of Compliance covers decks, additions and alterations that leave the building's use unchanged.
  • The department suggests obtaining one for any work done under a building permit.
  • Ask for the current fee before applying, since fees are set by building type.

A missing certificate is best resolved before listing, because a buyer's attorney is likely to ask for it.

sections.h2: Tax due dates and water bills at closing
sections.html:
Three payments fall due each year, and the last day of the due month is the cutoff. After that, interest runs at 1 percent per month, and the Finance Department cannot waive it.

  • July 1: first half of the city and school levy, late from August 1.
  • January 1: second half of the city and school levy, late from February 1.
  • April 1: the county levy, late from May 1.

Bills go out in mid-December, late March and June. Under Real Property Tax Law Section 922 a bill that fails to arrive changes nothing, so call the Finance Department at 914-422-1248 if yours is missing. Make checks payable to the Commissioner of Finance, 255 Main Street, Room 102.

Water adds a seller's task. A final reading costs $75 and is requested at 914-422-1211, and unpaid water charges come back onto the property as a tax lien on the following July 1. Ownership on the tax roll changes only after the Assessor's Office gets a certified copy of the recorded deed. Send it promptly, and file the city's Tax Account Change Form if the bill needs a new mailing address.

A cash buyer needs no mortgage approval and takes the house in its present condition, so there is no appraisal to fail and no repair list to negotiate. The tax calendar, the water reading, the Certificate of Occupancy and the deed filing still apply. Line those up first and the closing date is yours to set.

The Assessor's Office runs on a fixed yearly calendar, and the complaint window is short. December 1 is the taxable status date, the tentative roll is dated January 1, complaints are taken January 1 to 21, and the final roll lands on March 1. Exemptions are handled from April 1 through December 1.

One assessed value drives both the city and school bills, so a seller who finds it too high should collect recent nearby sales before January. The office is at 255 Main Street, phone 914-422-1223.

The state charges the seller a base transfer tax per $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500, and the buyer owes an added 1 percent when a residence sells for $1 million or more. Form TP-584 travels with the deed to the county clerk, and payment is due within 15 days of delivery.

The Westchester County Clerk's Land Records Division takes a deed only with four documents generated in its PREP system: a recording cover sheet, the TP-584, the RP-5217 transfer report and a payment cover sheet. Originals come back after scanning, and anyone needing a certified copy fast should order it with the submission.

The state transfer tax is $2 for each $500 of price. The seller pays unless the contract assigns it to the buyer.

faqs.q: Who is billed for White Plains tax after a sale?
faqs.a: The owner of record, until the Assessor's Office is sent a certified copy of the recorded deed. Send it promptly, and file the city's Tax Account Change Form if the bill needs a new mailing address.

faqs.q: Who pays state transfer tax on a White Plains sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays, unless the contract assigns it to the buyer. The tax is $2 for each $500 of price, rounded up to the next $500.

faqs.q: What if no White Plains tax bill arrives?
faqs.a: The tax and any interest are still owed. Call the Finance Department at 914-422-1248 to verify the address and request a duplicate.

faqs.q: When is the White Plains complaint window?
faqs.a: From January 1 to January 21 each year. The next one opens January 1, 2027, against the tentative roll.

faqs.q: Is a missing Certificate of Occupancy a problem for a White Plains sale?
faqs.a: It is best to resolve it first, since the city bars occupancy without one and a buyer's attorney is likely to ask. The route is a Building Short Form for an Updated and Substitute CO, then an inspection.
